dedupe_keys.name: quantifying the spatial homogeneity of urban road networks via graph neural networks

description: A Purdue University and Peking University team releases code for measuring homogeneity of urban road networks with graph neural networks. Zenodo archives a public source bundle under CC BY 4.0, and the linked GitHub repository identifies Python, NetworkX, OSMnx and PyTorch requirements under MIT. Its README describes road collection for 30 cities in the United States, Europe and Asia, intra-city link prediction, road classification and inter-city comparisons. Network-homogeneity indicators can help compare urban road topology before resilience or routing simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this method. A limitation is that a similarity or predictability score is not a measured traffic capacity or flood vulnerability; transferring it to service performance needs validation. The GitHub README names one paper DOI and Zenodo another journal-page DOI, so the describing article identity should be checked before citation. Neither archive nor training data was downloaded, and no link-prediction score was reproduced.
